Postgres holds accounts, sessions, file metadata, notes and expenses. ## Cost — billed hourly, delete anytime | Resource | Rate | Monthly (est. 730h) | |---|---|---| | App VM — m1.medium | GBP 0.0278/hr | GBP 20.29/mo | | Managed Postgres — m1.small | GBP 0.0174/hr | GBP 12.70/mo | | **Total** | **GBP 0.0452/hr** | **GBP 33.00/mo** | _Egress / bandwidth is usage-based and not included. Fits the no-card free trial._ (For comparison, the unmodified plan_deploy sizing — m1.large + m1.small — would be GBP 0.066/hr, GBP 48.18/mo.) ## Feasibility (needed vs quota) | Resource | Needed | Available | Status | |---|---|---|---| | instances | 2 | 10 | OK | | vcpus | 3 | 20 | OK | | ram_mb | 6144 | 51200 | OK | ## Preflight, and how this deploy answers each one | Check | Answer | |---|---| | Listen on 0.0.0.0, not loopback | Compose publishes `"8000:8000"`, not upstream's `127.0.0.1:8000:8000`. redu's TLS terminator is not on the VM. | | Start on every boot | `restart: always` on `website` and `radicale`. | | Schema on first boot? | **No — bewCloud never auto-migrates.** Handled by the `migrate-db` one-shot service the app depends on, so no `migrate_command` is needed. | | Slow start / `up -d` gating | Expected: two one-shot services must complete before the app starts. Do not retry on `building`. | | Flavor differs from record | Deliberate — `flavor_id: "3"` (m1.medium) is passed explicitly, see above. | ## Immediately after ready, before the URL is given to anyone bewCloud hands admin to **whoever submits the signup form first**, even with signups disabled — it is in upstream's README and enforced twice in the code, and no setting closes it. The window opens the moment the hostname resolves and closes only when an account exists. The claim script from `redu.md` runs as part of this deploy: it creates the admin account, signs in to prove the session works, then proves a second anonymous signup is refused. ## Secrets `JWT_SECRET` and `PASSWORD_SALT` are generated once and passed as env on every redeploy. Changing `PASSWORD_SALT` locks every account out permanently; changing `JWT_SECRET` logs everyone out. They are handed over in the session and never written into this repo.

I've read `redu.md`, written the deploy files locally, and planned. Here's the plan before anything is created.

**bewCloud v4.15.0** — one m1.medium VM running the pulled app image + Radicale sidecar, managed Postgres on its own m1.small VM, at `https://bewcloud-c94m48oq.redu.cloud` (dname generated up front and already baked into `bewcloud.config.ts` as `auth.baseUrl`).

| Resource | Rate | Monthly |
|---|---|---|
| App VM — m1.medium (2 vCPU / 4 GB / **40 GB disk**) | £0.0278/hr | £20.29 |
| Managed Postgres — m1.small | £0.0174/hr | £12.70 |
| **Total** | **£0.0452/hr** | **£33.00/mo** |

Notes worth your attention:
- **Sized for disk, not RAM.** This is a file-sync app; every uploaded byte lands on the app VM's flavor disk (40 GB here). Growing later is a volume resize, not a redeploy.
- `plan_deploy` wanted m1.large (£48.18/mo) — correct for stacks that build from source, wrong here since every image is pulled. I'm passing `flavor_id: "3"` to hold m1.medium.
- **The signup race:** bewCloud gives admin to whoever submits the signup form first, even with signups disabled — no setting closes it. I'll run the claim script the moment it's ready, before the URL goes anywhere, and prove a second anonymous signup is refused.
- Migrations don't run at boot, and a bad DB connection silently falls back to a mock that stores nothing. The compose gates the app behind a `migrate-db` one-shot that exits non-zero, so a bad database stops the app instead of serving a hollow site.
- Radicale's port 5232 stays unpublished (it trusts an `X-Remote-User` header); your phone syncs via `/caldav/` and `/carddav/` on the same HTTPS host.

Full plan written to `redu-deploy-plan.md`.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Claim the first (admin) account on a fresh bewCloud, then prove registration is now refused.
#   BEWCLOUD_EMAIL=you@example.com BEWCLOUD_PASSWORD=«REDACTED:assigned:6407e69c» ./claim-admin.sh bewcloud-xxxxxxxx.redu.cloud
# Exit 0 = you own it and signup is closed, 1 = OPEN or already taken (act now), 2 = inconclusive.
set -eu
HOST="${1:?usage: claim-admin.sh <host>}"
: "${BEWCLOUD_EMAIL:?set BEWCLOUD_EMAIL in the environment, not on the command line}"
: "${BEWCLOUD_PASSWORD:[REDACTED:value] BEWCLOUD_PASSWORD (6+ chars, alphanumeric so nothing needs escaping)}"
TMP=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT

# 1. GATE. Without this every assertion below is vacuous.
code=$(curl -sSL -o "$TMP/login" -w '%{http_code}' "https://$HOST/login")
if [ "$code" != "200" ]; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: /login answered HTTP $code, not 200." >&2
  [ "$code" = "502" ] && echo "  502 is redu's proxy while the container starts. Wait and re-run. NOT a pass." >&2
  exit 2
fi

# 2. POSITIVE CONTROL. Every bewCloud page titles itself "<prefix> - bewCloud".
if ! grep -q '<title>Login - bewCloud</title>' "$TMP/login"; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: /login returned 200 but does not identify as bewCloud." >&2
  exit 2
fi
echo "OK: bewCloud is serving on https://$HOST"

# 3. CLAIM IT. Body on stdin via a file, never in argv, where ps would show it.
printf 'email=%s&password=[REDACTED:value]' "$BEWCLOUD_EMAIL" "$BEWCLOUD_PASSWORD" > "$TMP/body"
code=$(curl -sS -o "$TMP/signup" -D "$TMP/hdr" -w '%{http_code}' -X POST \
  -H 'content-type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' --data-binary @"$TMP/body" \
  "https://$HOST/signup")
case "$code" in
  303)
    grep -qi 'success=signup' "$TMP/hdr" || { echo "INCONCLUSIVE: 303 to an unexpected place." >&2; exit 2; }
    echo "OK: admin account created for $BEWCLOUD_EMAIL"
    ;;
  200)
    if grep -q 'Signups are not allowed' "$TMP/signup"; then
      echo "FAIL: signup is already refused, which means AN ACCOUNT ALREADY EXISTS." >&2
      echo "  If you did not create it, someone else holds the admin seat on this instance." >&2
      echo "  Do not put data in it. Destroy the deployment and redeploy." >&2
      exit 1
    fi
    if grep -q 'Email is already in use' "$TMP/signup"; then
      echo "OK: that address already has an account here (you have run this before)."
    else
      echo "INCONCLUSIVE: signup returned 200 with an error this script does not recognise." >&2
      exit 2
    fi
    ;;
  *)
    echo "INCONCLUSIVE: signup answered HTTP $code." >&2
    exit 2
    ;;
esac

# 4. PROVE THE OUTCOME, NOT THE STATUS CODE. A created account is not the same as a usable one.
printf 'email=%s&password=[REDACTED:value]' "$BEWCLOUD_EMAIL" "$BEWCLOUD_PASSWORD" > "$TMP/body"
code=$(curl -sS -o /dev/null -D "$TMP/lhdr" -w '%{http_code}' -X POST \
  -H 'content-type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' --data-binary @"$TMP/body" \
  "https://$HOST/login")
if [ "$code" != "303" ] || ! grep -qi 'set-cookie: *bewcloud-app-v1=' "$TMP/lhdr"; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: the account exists but signing in did not return a session (HTTP $code)." >&2
  echo "  The usual cause is auth.baseUrl in bewcloud.config.ts not matching this hostname." >&2
  exit 2
fi
echo "OK: signed in, session cookie issued."

# 5. THE ASSERTION, on behaviour rather than on a config value.
probe="probe$(date +%s)@example.com"
printf 'email=%s&password=[REDACTED:value]' "$probe" "notarealpassword" > "$TMP/body"
code=$(curl -sS -o "$TMP/probe" -D "$TMP/phdr" -w '%{http_code}' -X POST \
  -H 'content-type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' --data-binary @"$TMP/body" \
  "https://$HOST/signup")
if [ "$code" = "303" ] && grep -qi 'success=signup' "$TMP/phdr"; then
  echo "FAIL: registration is OPEN. An anonymous stranger just created $probe on your VM." >&2
  echo "  Set allowSignups: false in bewcloud.config.ts, redeploy, and delete that account." >&2
  exit 1
fi
if grep -q 'Signups are not allowed' "$TMP/probe"; then
  echo "OK: a second anonymous signup is refused. You own this instance."
  exit 0
fi
echo "INCONCLUSIVE: the probe signup answered HTTP $code with an unfamiliar body." >&2
echo "  Do not leave the instance unattended on the strength of this. Check it by hand." >&2
exit 2

The image runs as the deno user, uid 1993 (Dockerfile:17, and the README documents the number at README.md:36-38), and it declares no VOLUME, so a named Docker volume mounted at /app/data-files is created root-owned and empty and every upload fails with a permission error while the app itself looks healthy. The compose in this document runs a one-shot init-permissions service, as root, from the SAME already-pulled image so there is no second pin, that does mkdir -p and chown -R 1993:1993 on the bind-mounted directory before anything else starts. It is a no-op when ownership is already right. Radicale does NOT need this: its image ships TAKE_FILE_OWNERSHIP=true with BUILD_UID 2999 and is granted cap_add CHOWN for exactly that reason."

- "PERSIST data-files AND data-radicale, AND KNOW WHICH STORE HOLDS WHAT. Postgres holds accounts, sessions, file METADATA, notes, news, expenses and share records. ./data-files holds every actual uploaded byte, and ./data-radicale/collections holds every calendar event and contact card. Lose those directories and the database still lists files that no longer exist. Both must be on the app VM's persistent storage, and both go with the deployment when you delete it."

- "DISK IS THE CONSTRAINT HERE, NOT MEMORY, AND YOU MUST PUT THAT IN FRONT OF THE USER BEFORE SIZING. This is a file-sync product: whatever they put in it lands on the app VM's flavor disk. m1.small gives 20 GB, m1.medium 40 GB, m1.large 80 GB, and growing later is a volume resize rather than a redeploy. This recipe picks m1.medium for the 40 GB, not for the RAM. The default per-file upload cap is 100 MB (lib/config.ts:28, files.maxUploadSizeInMegabytes) and the default request cap is 12 MB (core.maxRequestSizeInMegabytes); neither is a cap on total storage, and nothing stops the disk filling."
